title: queue_freeing a meshinstance with a local to scene material on it causes lag spikes.
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.6 beta 1, 2, 3, and release candidate 1
Not reproducible in: 4.5.1 on Steam, 4.6.dev1

### System information

Godot v4.6.rc1 - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 6GB (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8157) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10700 CPU @ 2.90GHz (16 threads) - 15.82 GiB memory

### Issue description

In the latest 4.6 release candidate and the previous betas, I've noticed a pretty painful lag spike occurs when instancing a meshinstance3D if both it's surface material override has local to scene turned on, and it queue_frees. As far as I can tell, this issue does not exist on 4.5.1 or 4.6 dev1, or maybe its a lot less noticeable. Theres more to it - as in the minimal reproduction project it can still happen in 4.5 while not happening in my full project, but this is all i could figure out.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2c9d40ec-468c-4d59-8c9b-051160a14756

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ed7cf9d-2fef-4c2e-a7dd-e624b3f03ddc

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07aa2384-a90d-4bfc-9911-f06d1d4fdc83

### Steps to reproduce

Make instances of a meshinstance3d that has an emission and alpha transparency enabled standard material with local to scene turned on, then have the meshinstance3d quickly queue_free itself via an autostarting timer.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[tmp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24648619/tmp.zip)
